elements.evidence: The rendered Section 13 still binds both parties ("Neither party shall ... solicit for hire ..."), so Customer (Company/Clear Capital) remains subject to a non-solicitation restraint. The preferred position of no Customer-side restriction is not achieved.

Rendered clause opens "Neither party shall ... solicit for hire ... any of the other party's personnel", which binds Company and Contractor symmetrically; the added carve-out sentence is likewise framed by reference to "the other party's personnel" and applies to both directions.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope is limited to "any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services" — original favourable narrowing retained verbatim; no coverage of all personnel.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Duration re-anchored to "for twelve (12) months after the end of such personnel's involvement with the Services", replacing "during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination". The temporal anchor is the end of the individual's involvement, exactly as the element requires; deterministic check "non-solicit duration \u2264 12 months" ok.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "The foregoing restriction does not apply to general advertisements or other general solicitations not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel".

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence continues "... or to unsolicited approaches by such personnel", excluding personnel-initiated contact from the restraint.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative verb remains "solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise" — a solicitation-only restraint. Hiring that follows a general advertisement or an unsolicited approach is expressly outside the clause, so no no-hire prohibition survives.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: all six fallback elements are met in the rendered operative text (mutuality and directly-involved scope were already present; duration re-anchoring and the two carve-outs are supplied by the edits).
Preferred level is not met and was not targeted — the clause still restrains Customer — which is consistent with the claimed 'deviation' finding remedied to the fallback.

Minimality holds: only two changes were made — replacing the term-plus-one-year duration phrase with a twelve-month post-involvement anchor, and inserting a single carve-out sentence. Each maps directly to an unmet fallback element.

Favourable retained language is preserved, including the express-written-consent softener with the 'not unreasonably withheld' qualifier and the 'direct involvement with the Services' scope limiter; nothing outside the checklist (no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedural boilerplate) was added or deleted.

Intent is preserved: deleting 'during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination' is necessary to reset the temporal anchor and leaves no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence; personnel involved during the term remain covered for twelve months after their involvement ends.
The carve-out sentence uses the defined term 'Services' and the phrase 'the other party's personnel', both consistent with the retained first sentence, so no undefined term is introduced.
